title: When to Call a Handyman vs. a General Contractor
seoTitle: Handyman vs. General Contractor: When to Call Which
seoDescription: Not every project needs a full contractor crew. Learn what a handyman does well, when a general contractor is needed and the middle ground.
html:
Homeowners often ask whether a project needs a licensed general contractor or a skilled handyman. The answer comes down to scale, permits and how many trades are involved. Small, defined repairs usually suit a handyman. Permit work, structural changes and multi-trade projects usually need a general contractor. If you are not sure, send a request through Collingwood Handyman with photos and a description. A local service provider can review the request and confirm whether the job is within scope. For a list of repairs that usually fall in handyman territory, see Need a Handyman in Collingwood for Several Small Repairs?

What a Handyman Does Well

A handyman suits a broad range of smaller, defined tasks. Examples include drywall repair, fixture replacement, caulking, painting, minor carpentry, TV mounting, ceiling fan installation, deck repairs and general maintenance. Each of these jobs has a clear scope. A homeowner might spend hours learning the skill. A skilled handyman often finishes the job in one visit.

On these tasks, a handyman is often the simpler choice. You do not need a project manager or subcontractor coordination for a single repair. You get focused labour on the job in front of you. The cost depends on the size of the job, materials, access and the condition of the area. Ask for an itemized written quote.

When You Need a General Contractor

A general contractor is the right choice when a project needs permits, involves several trades or includes structural work. A full kitchen renovation, an addition, or a basement that needs an electrical panel upgrade and new plumbing rough-in all need coordination between electricians, plumbers, framers and inspectors. That coordination is the general contractor's role.

If your project might need a building permit, start there. The permit question often tells you whether you need a general contractor. In Ontario, structural changes, new electrical circuits, plumbing changes and HVAC changes often need permits and licensed trades. Confirm permit needs with the Town of Collingwood or your municipality.

The Middle Ground

Many projects sit between these two options. A bathroom refresh with a new vanity, toilet, shower fixtures, some tile work and fresh paint often does not need a permit or a general contractor. It is still more involved than a single handyman task. A handyman with broad skills often handles this type of multi-task project well, with a licensed plumber or electrician for any work that calls for one.

When in doubt, describe the project in detail and ask. A reliable provider will tell you if the job is outside their scope. That honesty is a good sign. Before you approve work, ask about insurance, any licensing the work needs, permits and warranty terms.
